definitions.explanation: Loving someone, typically a child or pet, to an excessive or unhealthy degree. Carries a negative connotation of love that lacks objectivity or discipline.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祖父|そふ}→祖父：01452_sofu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{孫|まご}→孫：03731_mago⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{溺愛|できあい}⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My grandfather dotes on his grandchild.

examples.japanese: ⟦{息子|むすこ}→息子：00799_musuko⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{溺愛|できあい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧あまり、⟦{何|なん}→何〜：03100_nan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{買|か}い{与|あた}えてしまう。
examples.english: She dotes on her son so much that she ends up buying him everything.

examples.japanese: ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{溺愛|できあい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{自立|じりつ}→自立：13970_jiritsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{妨|さまた}げる→妨げる：12223_samatageru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It is said that a parent's excessive doting can hinder a child's independence.

notes:
USAGE:
Used as a noun or with ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧. Almost always carries a critical or cautionary nuance — the love described is seen as excessive or unhealthy. The kanji ⟦{溺|おぼ}れる→溺れる：02026_oboreru⟧ means "to drown," so the word literally evokes being drowned in love.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {溺愛|できあい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to dote excessively on)
- {溺愛|できあい}⟦ぶり→〜ぶり：28358_buri⟧ (the extent of one's doting)
- {子|こ}ども⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{溺愛|できあい}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to dote on one's child)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {可愛|かわい}⟦がる→〜がる：03089_garu⟧: to cherish — positive and natural affection without the negative connotation
- ⟦{甘|あま}やかす→甘やかす：06625_amayakasu⟧: to spoil — focusing on permissive parenting rather than the emotional intensity
